claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 5 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 5 years old and lives with you in the UK.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upbringing - meaning do you provide for his needs such as food, clothing, and other day-to-day expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm responsible for looking after Alex - I provide for all his needs like food, clothes, and everything else he needs day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. That's helpful information.

Now, **is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex is currently in hospital. He's in hospital abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. It's important to understand more about Alex's situation since he's in hospital abroad.

**How long has Alex been in hospital abroad, and are you still in the UK while he is there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure how long this will go on for exactly. As for whether I'm back in the UK or still abroad with him - I honestly don't know what to tell you about that at the moment. It's all quite uncertain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is an uncertain and difficult time for you. Let me ask one more question to help clarify the situation:

**Did Alex go abroad specifically to receive hospital treatment, or was he already abroad for other reasons when he became ill and was hospitalized?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that either - whether he only went abroad for the hospital treatment or if there were other reasons. It's hard to say at this point.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about the uncertainties in your situation. I understand this is a difficult time.

Let me ask one final question: **Has Alex been in hospital for more than 12 weeks continuously?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't really know exactly how long it's been to be honest. The whole situation has been quite overwhelming and I haven't been keeping exact track of the weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is clearly a very stressful situation for you and your family.

Based on our conversation, let me summarize what we know about your situation with Alex:

- Alex is 5 years old and normally lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for his care and provide for all his needs
- He is currently in hospital abroad
- However, there are several key details that are uncertain, including:
  - How long Alex has been in hospital
  - Whether you are currently in the UK or abroad with him
  - Whether Alex went abroad specifically for hospital treatment or for other reasons

Unfortunately, without this information, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit. The rules for children in hospital abroad are specific: you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit if Alex only went abroad to be in hospital, you're back in the UK, and you're regularly spending money on him. Additionally, if a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks, this affects entitlement.

Given the uncertainties in your situation, I would recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly. They can discuss your specific circumstances in detail and provide guidance based on all the facts of your case.

Let me record my assessment now.
